rationale: Byakuya Kuchiki lands in Tier C because the kit's payoff doesn't keep pace with the investment it asks for — they can still carry specific content, but stronger options usually want the same resources. As a Tactician, the value here is control and setup as much as raw damage — the recommendations favor consistency and uptime over pure hit size. The Slash damage type also matters here: content weak to it is where this build over-performs its tier, and content resistant to it is where you should bench accordingly.

The recommended set — Blooming Sakura (3) — is chosen for how the set bonus lines up with the kit's actual damage profile, not because it's generically strong. Main stats go 1: Slash DMG > ATK%  •  2: Crit Rate  •  3: ATK% > Ult Charge Rate for the same reason: they feed what the kit multiplies. Crit DMG and Crit Rate lead the substat priority because they multiply together — once Crit Rate is high enough to land reliably, every point of Crit DMG scales the whole kit, which flat ATK can't match. Tactician who does not provide counters.

We call B0 the stopping point because that's where the boundary curve bends: the levels up to it unlock the pieces the kit is actually balanced around, while the levels past it mostly buy stat percentages at dupe prices.
The featured rotation ("Opener") is ordered the way it is to stack the kit's multipliers before the big hits land — the sequence matters more than the buttons. Use Battlefield on cooldown.

As with everything on this page, these calls come from community testing plus the wiki's numbers — when the data changes (balance patches, new stamps, better testing), the recommendations and this reasoning get updated together.
